entries.title: Bulls have sneaky depth with a few outsiders trying to crack rotation
entries.summary: <p>Tiago Splitter couldn’t explain why Noa Essengue seemed to spend a majority of his Summer League minutes knocked down on the hardwood rather than upright and showing promise in Year 2.</p><p>It obviously irked the new Bulls head coach, however, evident by the fact that he had no problem benching the 2025 first-round pick.</p><p>An early message being sent to the 19-year-old Frenchman?</p><p>Absolutely. As Essengue found out the new-look front office and Splitter have no allegiance to the old regime’s No. 12 overall selection. Yes, Splitter acknowledged that Essengue was coming off season-ending shoulder surgery that basically made his rookie campaign a red-shirt year but wasn’t about to get caught up in the excuse game for the forward.</p><p>“He’s got to maybe bring a little more force in everything he does,” Splitter said. “That’s something we’re working on.”</p><p>What if it’s just not in Essengue’s nature?</p><p>“Yeah, we’re going to keep pushing him,” Splitter replied.</p><p>To Essengue’s credit he did seem to hear the message, coming out of Las Vegas with an understanding that he needs to be less emotional and more tenacious. According to a source, two traits that irked the new staff.</p><p>“I am going to take a lot of contact,” Essengue told reporters. “So keep playing, know it’s gonna be like that in the NBA. You are a rookie and rookies never are going to get a call. So you try to keep playing until maybe one day you do get a call.</p><p>“I feel better, honestly, from the first game. (Splitter) told me he wants more energy offensively and told me to be more of a leader, talk more on defense.”</p><p>Boxes that Essengue never really checked. That’s why he will enter training camp on the outside looking in when it comes to the rotation and what the new-look roster will look like.</p><p></p><p><b>THE STARTERS:</b></p><p></p><p>Josh Giddey – For some odd reason it’s been open season on Giddey throughout the social media circuit this summer. What’s being overlooked is Giddey has the positional size that vice president of basketball operations Bryson Graham covets and would be a great fit for a lob game that Matas Buzelis, Caleb Wilson and Nic Claxton bring.</p><p></p><p>Norman Powell – The veteran was a bucket last season, becoming a first-time All-Star, and will be one of the true floor spacers in the starting lineup, shooting 40-plus% three of the last five seasons.</p><p></p><p>Caleb Wilson – The rookie showed in Las Vegas that he actually has the potential to play more like a three than a four, but either way he will be interchangeable with Matas Buzelis in the starting frontcourt. If he can be a threat from outside, however, that changes what this Bulls starting offense will look like instantly.</p><p></p><p>Matas Buzelis – It’s Year 3 for Buzelis as he continues – in his own words – hunting down being great. On paper, Buzelis and Wilson have a chance to be two of the brightest frontcourt stars in the Eastern Conference for the next five years.</p><p></p><p>Nic Claxton – Set screens, rim-run and be a defensive force around the rim. The job description for Claxton is a simple one and if his back holds up he should be able to fill it perfectly.</p><p></p><p><b>THE BENCH:</b></p><p></p><p>Tre Jones – The consummate pros pro, Jones will anchor the second unit as the ultimate floor general. Splitter will love the steadiness in which he plays.</p><p></p><p>Isaac Okoro – It’s easy to forget what Okoro brought to the Bulls last season, usually assigned the task of trying to slow down the opposing team’s best scorer. Now he will get a chance to do that for the second unit, becoming a leading trade candidate because of his expiring contract.</p><p></p><p>Leonard Miller – Throw the film on the last six weeks of the season and it’s clear that Miller outplayed Patrick Williams in almost every category. Training camp will be an interesting battle between the two.</p><p></p><p>Jalen Smith – The veteran had a great season last year, spacing the floor and playing like a true stretch-four.</p><p></p><p>Zach Collins – The Bulls brought Collins back for a reason and that’s because of his physicality in the paint. Another player Splitter will really like off the bench as long as Collins is healthy.</p><p></p><p><b>OUTSIDE LOOKING IN:</b></p><p></p><p>Rob Dillingham – There were some definite moments from Dillingham late last season and the fact that he’s been working out with Powell this summer says a lot about his dedication to improving.</p><p></p><p>Dailyn Swain – The rookie will need a lot of minutes in practice and the preseason to crack the rotation, so stay tuned on that front.</p><p></p><p>Patrick Williams – Yes, it is a new regime, but the film doesn’t lie. Williams needs to change some minds and make an impression right away rather than just float along.</p><p></p><p>Noa Essengue – His best basketball is in front of him, but that might be in the G League to start the season.</p>

entries.title: Shoppers left stranded as Save A Lot grocery stores in Chicago permanently close: ‘We have to eat, too’
entries.summary: <p>As shelves at the Save A Lot in West Lawn began to empty, Gladys Roman filled her shopping cart with whatever she could find to get her through the next few weeks.</p><p>Roman walked out of the store with a cart full of frozen meat, canned goods, juice and cooking oil — all for a fraction of what she would normally spend on a grocery haul of that size.</p><p>But the feeling was bittersweet.</p><p>“The people who shop here are on a budget,” said Roman, 64.</p><p>Roman was one of many shoppers who stopped by the store hours before it was set to permanently close on Saturday.</p><p>Save A Lot announced this week it was ending its licensing agreement with embattled operator Yellow Banana, which meant it had to find an alternative or <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/money/2026/07/21/save-a-lot-stores-set-to-close-saturday-after-years-of-turmoil-recent-ceo-death-threatens-city-funded-deal" target="_blank" >shutter all of its Save A Lot stores</a> Saturday, just a few years after promising to address food deserts in Chicago’s South and West sides. The closures will leave some predominantly Black and Brown neighborhoods without a grocery store for miles.</p><p>On Saturday morning, the store in West Lawn, which opened last year, had several empty shelves and no fresh produce. Many of the items left over were discounted at least 50%.</p><p>Some shoppers left the store with carts full of groceries, while others walked out empty-handed when they couldn’t find what they were looking for.</p><p>Loretta Claiborne took advantage of the discounts and stocked up on nonperishable items like cups, utensils, plates and napkins. She spent about $50 on a cart full of groceries. But the 78-year-old said she was disappointed to hear all the stores were closing.</p><p>Claiborne typically shops at the Save A Lot in Auburn Gresham, which is only a few blocks from her home. She said that location is frequented by seniors who don’t have a way to drive or are disabled.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure closing down.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Pat Nabong/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>An employee who did not want to be named said he’s worked at Save A Lot for more than 22 years. “Now I’m out of work,” he said.</p><p>Save A Lot did not respond to a request for comment. </p><p>“Financial headwinds” under Yellow Banana’s ownership led to the termination of the relationship, said Save A Lot spokesperson Sarah Griffin, pointing to “dramatic cuts to SNAP benefits” as a significant challenge.</p><p>Save A Lot was unable to find a path forward to keep the stores open and notified Yellow Banana at the end of June that it would terminate its operational agreement.</p><p>Ohio-based Yellow Banana has a $26 million redevelopment agreement with the city of Chicago, through which it received more than <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/business/2024/05/29/save-a-lot-yellow-banana-grocery-stores-delays-south-side-gresham" target="_blank" >$13 million in taxpayer financing</a> to renovate and reopen Save A Lot locations. The remaining funding came from federal grants and loans.</p><p>In addition to that taxpayer funding, Save A Lot has requested $3 million more from the city to recoup money given to Yellow Banana, Ald. Marty Quinn (13th) told the Sun-Times. Quinn said Save A Lot told him last week that the stores were in danger of closing.</p><p>Roman said she would be reaching out to Quinn’s office to find out what was being done to help residents in the neighborhood.</p><p>“Hopefully, [Quinn] can bring a good department store over here for the neighborhood,” she said.</p><p>With the stores closing, “the city is exploring every opportunity to recoup taxpayer funding, if necessary,” Department of Planning and Development spokesperson Peter Strazzabosco previously told the Sun-Times.</p>

entries.title: Why thousands packed Wrigley Field for the Savannah Bananas game — even those who dislike baseball
entries.summary: <p>Mary Miske, Diana Tabor and Priscilla Jones all “hate baseball.”</p><p>Yet, the three women stood outside Wrigley Field near Clark and Addison Saturday afternoon decked out in gear supporting the Savannah Bananas’ opposing team, the Firefighters. They wore red flame sunglasses, cowboy hats and gave out Fireball cinnamon whiskey shots out of a fake fire hose (only to adults).</p><p>Why did they come if they hate baseball so much?</p><p>Because they love Banana Ball — the high-energy, entertainment-focused and fan-first version of baseball <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/entertainment-culture/2025/08/14/savannah-bananas-guaranteed-rate-field" >made famous by the Savannah Bananas</a>.</p><p>“It’s what everybody loves about baseball and then they take what everybody hates about baseball out. ... It’s just the fun, the dancing, the crowd engagement. It’s incredible what he’s done,” said Tabor, 46, referring to Savannah Bananas owner Jesse Cole.</p><p>Tabor, who is Miske’s sister and is visiting from Texas, said all the fun is “not just the game, but the camaraderie before.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-7b0000" </div><p>So, why dress up in the opposing team’s colors?</p><p>“Because we look better in red than we do in yellow,” said Miske, 61, from Lake Zurich.</p><p>Over in right field, near Addison Street and Sheffield Avenue, David Weinberg was handing out bananas from a yellow-painted trash can with googly eyes and a home-plate-shaped face.</p><p>The 43-year-old Oak Forest artist bought about 60 pounds worth of bananas from Costco, loaded them into his yellow garbage can and handed them out to fans streaming into the sold-out Bananas game.</p><p>“Every time, I try to repurpose something because the whole concept of my trash art is to say that even though it’s trash, it still has life in it because it can be repurposed,” said Weinberg, dressed in a yellow T-shirt, yellow overalls and a baseball helmet he painted with various designs, including a Cubs “W” flag, ivy, and, of course, a banana on front.</p><p>Weinberg also set up a scavenger hunt with his art, scattering mini trash entries.title: 'A ray of sunshine with basketballs': WNBA All-Star Weekend lights up Chicago
entries.summary: <p>“Oh, it was beautiful — a ray of sunshine with basketballs,” Lyric Williams said. “I met Rickea Jackson. I saw Paige Bueckers. We took pictures with Flau’jae Johnson.”</p><p>The 16-year-old Chicagoan described her experience at WNBA Live, the league’s annual fan festival that transformed McCormick Place into a celebration of women’s basketball during the WNBA’s 30th anniversary All-Star Weekend.</p><p>But WNBA Live was only one part of the celebration. More than 30 fan experiences filled the convention hall, from basketball challenges and player appearances to custom Nike sneaker stations, Coach’s commemorative keychain engraving, wine tastings and the league’s interactive Legacy Park exhibit, where tens of thousands of fans explored three decades of WNBA history while learning about the “Line ’Em Up” initiative to paint orange three-point lines on public basketball courts nationwide.</p><p>Among the fans was the McMichael family from Calumet City.</p><p>Twelve-year-old Shiann McMichael and her 10-year-old sister, Londyn, joined one of the winding lines inside the orange-and-white convention hall, blending into a sea of team jerseys. Shiann wore the silver-and-black No. 22 jersey of Aces star A’ja Wilson, while Londyn sported former Sky star Angel Reese’s jersey.</p><p>“This experience means a lot to me because I get to see all the players that showed me how to play basketball,” Shiann said.</p><p>Shiann and Londyn’s father, Law McMichael, said bringing the event to Chicago was “something big” for the city.</p><p>“Chicago gets a lot of bad rep with the violence and sports organizations,” Law said. “Maybe this is a break from the norm so people can forget about that stuff for a few days.”</p><p>WNBA Live, held Thursday through Saturday, gave fans opportunities to meet players including Kamilla Cardoso, Courtney Williams, Sydney Colson and Johnson, compete in skills challenges and celebrate the league’s milestone season.</p><p>Andersonville resident Erin Carson has been a fan of the league for nearly five years. She decided to bring her sons to WNBA Live to expose them to women’s basketball.</p><p>“It’s important for them to see that women can do all the same things that they can do, and there’s a lot of amazing females,” Carson said.</p><p>Carson wasn’t sure what to expect, but the event exceeded those expectations.</p><p>“It’s massive, it’s set up really well, there’s so many basketball players walking around and trying to make a name for themselves,” Carson said. “The W[NBA] is doing really great things.”</p><p>The celebration extended beyond McCormick Place. On Thursday, the WNBA became the first professional sports league to host public events at the newly opened Obama Presidential Center. The day’s programming included All-Star practice, an appearance by former President Barack Obama and a Jr. WNBA skills clinic featuring four-time MVP Wilson. The league and the Sky also announced plans to paint 30 orange three-point lines on Chicago’s public courts this year — including 15 during All-Star Weekend — as part of the nationwide initiative.</p><p>Williams, a rising junior at King College Prep, participated in the Jr. WNBA clinic Thursday at the center’s Home Court gym, where more than 150 girls received a pair of Wilson’s signature A’Two shoes.</p><p>“Chicago is a great city with a lot of talent, especially in CPS [Chicago Public Schools] and even in the suburbs,” Williams said. “It’s just so much talent, and for it to be recognized with the WNBA coming here is amazing.”</p><p>Fans watched Wings rookie Azzi Fudd win the three-point contest Friday at Wintrust Arena.</p><p>But beyond the trophies and highlight reels, the weekend marked a milestone for a league that spent much of its early history fighting for stability and visibility. Thirty years later, record attendance, soaring television audiences, expansion franchises and increased investment have transformed the WNBA’s trajectory. As the league celebrated its past in Chicago, the focus was just as much on what comes next.</p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" entries.title: Fueled by NLDS loss to Brewers, Cubs relish chance to turn regular season’s ‘dog days’ into playoff momentum
entries.summary: <p>PITTSBURGH – If these are the dog days of the season, consider the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> a bunch of energetic Jack Russell terriers.</p><p>The vibes were detectably high after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/24/game-saving-defense-fires-up-cubs-in-thick-of-division-race-were-at-that-point-every-game-matters" >Friday night’s win over the Pirates</a>, an extra-inning nailbiter with a division foe fighting for one of the playoff spots the Cubs currently own. It was the type of performance necessary to win in October.</p><p>And though it’s still July, that’s what the Cubs – who fell to the division-rival Brewers in the NLDS last year – are itching to do: win in October.</p><p>“That taste that we had in our mouth after losing Game 5 in the DS? To get to that point and go further, the opportunity lies in front of us,” Boyd said Saturday. “We’re excited about that.</p><p>“The Brewers played better than us over the course of five games, yet we know where our talent stands. We know where we can go and what we can do.</p><p>“It didn’t end how we wanted it to. It doesn’t mean it wasn’t a great year. … However, it does light a hunger in you, and that’s what’s exciting, to get the opportunity to go, ‘OK, if we really want to do what we want to do and grow off that experience, it’s right in front of us.’”</p><p>The teams the Cubs are up against on their current road trip, the Pirates and Cardinals, are chasing their own postseason goals. Then comes a home stand featuring high-profile series with the Yankees and Dodgers.</p><p>Facing off against Pirates ace Paul Skenes on Saturday, the Cubs saw the kind of pitcher they’ll be up against in the playoffs.</p><p>These might be the dog days for some, particularly after the trade deadline passes, but the Cubs see the road to the World Series right in front of them. They’re ready to hit the gas.</p><p>“You hear ‘dog days.’ You can look at it a few different ways,” Boyd said. “The excitement of what stands beyond, in terms of where we want to go as a team, it’s right there, it’s palpable. You can taste it.</p><p>“The Pirates are a very good team. … The Cardinals are right there, too. We’re playing the Dodgers. We’re playing the Yankees. We have good opponents when the games matter, and it’s awesome to play those games, because they’re the teams you want to be playing against – that you will be playing against – when you get to where you want to go.”</p><p>If the Cubs are going to get past a Brewers-shaped roadblock, Boyd will be a big part of the equation.</p><p>An All Star last season, he was disappointed to miss as much time as he did in the first half this season, on the IL twice, including for the better part of two months while recovering from knee surgery.</p><p>But since returning, he’s been fantastic, with a 2.31 ERA in six starts, including the seven innings of one-run ball he logged Friday.</p><p>Jed Hoyer’s front office <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/17/cubs-mlb-trade-deadline-rumors-starting-pitching-jed-hoyer-front-office" >will be searching for pitching</a> before the Aug. 3 trade deadline, but the Cubs <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/01/cubs-matthew-boyd-all-star-ace-starting-rotation-pitching-injuries-craig-counsell-pete-crow-armstrong-alex-bregman-thumbs-down" >might have an in-house ace</a> in Boyd, who’s helping stabilize an injury-ravaged staff.</p><p>“We’ve lost so much talent, from that perspective,” manager Craig Counsell said Friday, “but Matt, you feel like he’s gotten us some back, coming back and pitching games like this.”</p><p>Leaning on Boyd last year against the Brewers backfired, with the lefty making his second start of the postseason on short rest in Game 1 of the NLDS, giving up six runs and only recording two outs.</p><p>The Cubs know, as Boyd said last month, that <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/06/28/cubs-brewers-series-nl-central-standings-pitching-injuries-craig-counsell-matthew-boyd" >“the Central runs through” the Brewers</a>. They also know what they’re capable of and haven’t shied away from championship-level expectations.</p><p>“We know how good we are. We know what we do well. We do things well that a lot of other teams don’t,” Boyd said. “That’s not comparing ourselves to other teams, we just know how good we are at what we do.</p><p>“What makes us a team is being true to our identity, not trying to go be some other team. There’s a lot of confidence in that, and the confidence only grows with the days that come.”</p>
entries.author: Vinnie Duber

entries.title: Despite sporadic power, White Sox say Braden Montgomery is "in a good spot"
entries.summary: <p><b>Braden Montgomery </b><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/06/10/braden-montgomery-white-sox-walk-off-home-run-steve-stone-bob-costas-will-venable-colson-montgomery" >used his power</a> to provide one of the most memorable moments of the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> season when he marked his June 9 major-league debut with a walk-off home run against the Braves.</p><p>Other than that, Montgomery’s muscle has largely been absent. Entering Saturday, Montgomery was slugging .409 with a 58.1% ground ball percentage and pulling the ball at only a 26.7% rate.</p><p>The Sox are still confident Montgomery’s power will re-emerge.</p><p>“To see him go out there and grind and use the whole field is awesome,” manager <b>Will Venable </b>said. “But there's a version of him which is exciting, which he's going to be pulling the ball hard in the air and doing some damage. He's going to work toward that but for right now, he's in a good spot.”</p><p>That he is, and there are even some signs the power is creeping back.</p><p>Montgomery had three hits Friday night, and over his last eight games was slashing .344/.382/.563 with a home run, two doubles and a triple. Venable said Montgomery is being more athletic with his lower half, allowing him to meet the ball.</p><p>"We're seeing a lot of quality at-bats from Braden and it's really about him working to get on time,” Venable said. “He’s just got such aptitude and works so hard. It's been really cool to watch him figure out what adjustments he needs to make and then go out and do it.”</p><h2>Help from below?</h2><p>The Sox are expected to add pitching before the Aug. 3 trade deadline to bolster a staff that entered Saturday 11th in baseball with a 4.13 ERA but with clear needs in both the rotation and bullpen.</p><p>They will also need reinforcements from within their system, and there are pitchers in the minors who have contributed to the Sox. <b>Drew Thorpe </b>is working his way back from 2025 Tommy John surgery, <b>Jonathan Cannon </b>pitched six innings of one-run ball Friday for Triple-A Charlotte and 2025 All-Star and this year’s Opening Day starter <b>Shane Smith </b>is also in Charlotte.</p><p>Those are just three examples of potential additions but any new blood would have to be sharp if called upon.</p><p>“It's really important we get those guys dialed in,” Venable said.</p><h2>When there’s a Will…</h2><p>The Sox are in the American League playoff race but that isn’t impacting how Venable is managing the team.</p><p>Venable said he and the Sox are trying to find a path to win every game, and that the first game of the year is just as important as the rest that have followed.</p><p>“We are just going out and trying to find a way, so nothing has changed other than where we are at currently, which we know doesn’t mean a whole lot,” Venable said. “Right now, we are just focused on what we can do to win tonight and that’s the same as any other day this season.”</p><h2>Crisis averted</h2><p>Double-A Birmingham infielder <b>Caleb Bonemer</b>, the Sox’ top prospect and 16th overall per MLB Pipeline, did not suffer a concussion when he was hit in the head with a pitch during the third inning Friday night.</p><p>Bonemer, however, was not in the Barons’ starting lineup Saturday.</p>
entries.author: Brian Sandalow

entries.title: Bears CB Kyler Gordon, LB T.J. Edwards among 6 players put on injured lists
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> likely will begin training camp without several key players.</p><p>They put linebacker T.J. Edwards on the Non-Football Injury list and nickel cornerback <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/06/03/bears-kyler-gordon-ben-johnson-injury-spoils-offseason-springboard-joint-practice-rams-myles-garrett-nfl" >Kyler Gordon</a> and defensive end Shemar Turner on the Physically Unable to Perform list.</p><p>Any of them could be activated by the time the Bears hold their first practice Wednesday, and teams sometimes use those lists as a precaution. Rookies and quarterbacks reported Saturday.</p><p>Edwards is coming back from a broken leg he suffered late last season and is expected to be ready relatively soon.</p><p>Turner’s situation is less clear coming off a torn ACL midway through last season, and Gordon was dealing with a soft-tissue issue during Organized Team Activities and minicamp. Gordon’s injury is concerning after he missed 14 games because of three injuries last season.</p><p>The Bears also put left tackle Ozzy Trapilo, who likely will miss most or all of the season with a knee injury on PUP, along with rookie linebacker Keyshawn Elliott and backup linebacker Noah Sewell.</p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser
